caption: why is he collecting villagers 🛶
logline: A villager kid gets in a player's boat and is dragged out of her village across the grass; he calls her number forty, he already took her Mom and her uncle, and none of them came back, so she's sure they love it there; at dusk her boat bumps the old empty village across the water and Mom, her uncle and the old librarian who was alone for years are waiting, the village lit behind them.
question: why tf is this man dragging a villager kid across the grass in a boat?
premise: A player pulls a baby villager out of Oakend in an oak boat on a lead, across the grass. He calls her number forty. He took her Mom last week and her uncle before that, and none came back, so today she got in the boat and waited. The first time he came, he looked across the water at the old empty village, where one light was on, and said someone's been alone a long time.
twist: Every Minecraft player knows a villager dragged in a boat is going to a trading hall. He isn't building one. He is filling Fernbank, the empty village across the inlet where the old librarian has lived alone with the golem for years, one villager at a time: number forty is the fortieth neighbour he has brought her. At dusk the boat bumps the dock, every window is lit, and Mom and the uncle are waiting at the dock's foot beside the librarian. 'None of them came back. They must love it there' was true.
payoff_note: the cut to S11 lands on EMPTY (the picture contradicts the word); S11 holds 1.2 s after L10 ends; the Short ends there. No line after L10, no gap shot (critic r1 must-fix 6).

lines.text: A PLAYER / pulled me out / of my VILLAGE / in a BOAT. / Across the GRASS.
lines.say: A player pulled me out of my village in a boat. Across the grass.
lines.direction: delighted, one quick breath, telling a friend the best news; the last word lands
lines.note: 'player' (critic r1 should-fix): sets up the trading-hall read and keeps the out-of-context read of a strange man and a little girl off the hook

lines.text: He calls me / number FORTY. / He's GOOD / at COUNTING.
lines.say: He calls me number forty. He's good at counting.
lines.note: 0a: 'number forty' misread as a skill (he is counting the villagers he has carried home, not stock for a hall)

lines.direction: pure joy, bouncing with the boat
lines.note: 0a: the kid thinks a boat dragged over grass is a fun ride (players know it is how villagers are moved to trading halls)

lines.text: The FIRST time he came, / he looked across the WATER / at the old / EMPTY village. / Somebody left / ONE light ON.
lines.say: The first time he came, he looked across the water at the old empty village. Somebody left one light on.
lines.direction: storytelling, bright, the last bit a shrug of a fact
lines.note: must-change 1 (premise) and critic r1 must-fixes 1-3: a flashback (graded), so the village really was empty and dark then; 'Somebody left ONE light ON' is the kid's misreading of the lit window (0a); S04 on most of the line, the cut to S04b's long lens on ON (the librarian alone at her lit west window)

lines.text: Someone's been ALONE / a long TIME.
lines.say: Someone's been alone a long time.
lines.direction: plain, normal volume, to himself, looking away across the water
lines.note: the man's one line (must-change 1), on screen while he says it; critic r1 must-fix 7: plain, never low and tender (the out-of-context read)

lines.text: I think / he means HIMSELF. / He doesn't have / any FRIENDS.
lines.say: I think he means himself. He doesn't have any friends.
lines.direction: sure of it, sweet, a little sorry for him
lines.note: 0a: the kid's innocent misreading of 'someone' (it is the old librarian across the water)

lines.text: He took MOM / last WEEK. / And my UNCLE / before THAT.
lines.say: He took Mom last week. And my uncle before that.
lines.direction: bright, a fun fact, no worry at all
lines.note: the turn: for a player this is the dark beat (a man taking a family one by one); S07 on MOM, S07b on UNCLE

lines.text: None of them / came BACK. / They must / LOVE it there. / So TODAY, / I got in the BOAT / and WAITED.
lines.say: None of them came back. They must love it there. So today, I got in the boat and waited.
lines.direction: cheerful and certain, then proud of her own plan
lines.note: 0a: 'They must LOVE it there' (a player reads cells; literally true). Critic r1 should-fix (agency): she chose the boat (vanilla: a mob walking into a boat gets in)

lines.text: At the WATER, / he got in his OWN boat, / and mine came / RIGHT behind. / My boat finally / got to SWIM!
lines.say: At the water, he got in his own boat, and mine came right behind. My boat finally got to swim!
lines.direction: giggling, the best part of the trip
lines.note: critic r1 must-fix 4 answered the vanilla way: she got in first, and a mob in a boat's front seat means a player can't steer it, so he rows his own boat and tows hers on the lead (a lead works while the holder rides; it does nothing only while a player sits in the LED boat). Engine check: test it

lines.text: When it got DARK, / we bumped into / the old / EMPTY village.
lines.say: When it got dark, we bumped into the old empty village.
lines.direction: a little slower, curious, still happy; the last word a small wonder
lines.note: the reveal on EMPTY: the cut to S11 lands on the word (critic r1 must-fix 6: one shot, Mom, the librarian and Uncle with the lit village behind); held 1.2 s after the line; the kid says nothing about what the picture shows
